svg.title: How the estimated break-even age changes as a cohort matures
svg.desc: For the same cohort, conditional break-even-age bands and the separate probability of no break-even update as observations arrive; hidden simulated outcomes provide a reference. Two equally priced fictional source worlds start with the same prelaunch prior and follow the same fixed day-70 cohort. At each cutoff the model is refit using only then-visible observations, and predicts that cohort under hold-current future conditions. The top panel shows first-break-even age quantiles only among predictive paths that cross zero by age 425: darker fill is the middle 50%, pale fill the middle 80%, and solid line the median. Dashed lines show evaluator-only hidden outcomes for context. The lower panel reports predictive paths with no break-even by age 425. These are posterior predictive intervals, not a promise that uncertainty shrinks monotonically: new evidence can shift or widen the estimate, and future process variation remains. Both sources have the same $0.05 per-lead price; the difference is hidden subscriber performance.
